question: Why did the EXP-018 off-machine hop run at 1.8-3.5 MB/s, and what does cross-site replication actually cost?

topology.workstation: macOS, in Japan for these measurements (nearest DERP Tokyo; hard NAT, no port mapping)
topology.sf_site: RTX 4090 and RTX 3090 hosts behind one easy NAT with UPnP/NAT-PMP/PCP
topology.nyc_site: RTX 5090 host; replicas live on its WSL distro's ext4

workstation-sf.note: heavy queueing delay; 0% loss over 30 pings

paths.relay_observation: the RTX 4090 host's path to the workstation was relayed via DERP while idle and upgraded to direct after a few pings; the RTX 3090 host was direct and just as slow, so the relay did not set the EXP-018 rate

corrected_causes: The EXP-018 hop crossed the Pacific twice: the workstation was in Japan, and its path to SF queues to 900 ms RTT under load. The fleet's own path (NYC<->SF, 67 ms) was never measured that night.
A single ssh stream is bound by the SSH channel window (about 1.6 MB in flight): 8-14 MB/s at 67-190 ms whatever the link. Parallel ranged streams scale it.
The workstation's ssh_config set `Compression yes` globally, so zero-filled test files looked 10x faster than real checkpoint payloads. Removed; pscp.py also forces Compression=no.

The export's 158 s was tar's 10 KiB record size against the 9p bounce, not 9p itself: `tar -b 8192` writes 2.6 GB to /mnt/c in 9.1 s (287 MB/s) against 72.8 s (37.6 MB/s), and the export itself is 4.9 s for 2.74 GB.

Windows OpenSSH cannot carry bulk between two Windows hosts: ssh.exe acting as a client inside an sshd session stalls on any large binary stream (measured: a single 8 MiB ranged read did not complete in 240 s, whatever the sender). Both output handles being anonymous pipes hangs it outright; file-backed handles fix the small commands but not bulk. wsl.exe also stalls on binary stdout, so a WSL-resident file cannot be served through the Windows sshd.

The first ranged-HTTP implementation probed the file size with a bodied GET and abandoned it, so the server wrote the whole file into a socket nobody read: every fetch moved the payload twice. Fixed to HEAD (schema 1 of this receipt reported 7.1 MB/s under that bug).

measurements.method: scp single stream, 256 MB zeros, ssh Compression=yes
8 parallel ranged ssh reads, 256 MB zeros, Compression=yes
1 ranged ssh read, 1 GB random, Compression=no
8 parallel ranged ssh reads, 1 GB random, Compression=no
scp single stream from ext4, 256 MB random
measurements.note: Linux sshd sender, same link as the 2.2 MB/s Windows-sshd figure

measurements.method: single TCP stream over the tailnet (HTTP), 1 GB random
8 independent curl processes over the tailnet, 8 x 1 GB
ranged HTTP, 16 streams, 1.13 GB checkpoint archive (HEAD fix)
ranged HTTP, 16 streams, 1.13 GB checkpoint archive
measurements.note: same link, Linux receiver: the Windows receiver is the asymmetry, not the path

measurements.method: tar with default 10 KiB records, ext4 -> /mnt/c (9p), 2.74 GB
tar -b 8192 (4 MiB records), same replica and mount
checkpoint_sync.py export of a 2.74 GB session in the helper container
sha256 in the helper container, single payload file

conclusions: Replicate to a Linux endpoint wherever possible: the same 67 ms link carries 11.5 MB/s into a Windows host and 56-63 MB/s into WSL ext4 with the identical tool and stream count.
Use ranged HTTP with 16 streams for cross-site bulk (scripts/hosts/pscp.py serve/fetch, bearer token, tailnet only, SHA-256 verified); use ssh only where one end is not Windows.
A 4.35 GB RTX 5090 replica now leaves the machine in about 25 s of local work (export 10.7 s, tar 15 s) plus the transfer, and comes back in 69 s.
The EXP-018 receipts' import and restore timings are unaffected: they are local-disk figures.
host_changes_made: workstation ssh_config: global `Compression yes` removed (backup at ~/.ssh/config.bak-20260906)

the RTX 5090 host WSL sshd: moved from loopback :22 (which collided with the Windows sshd through mirrored networking and left the socket unit failed since 2026-07-28) to loopback :2222, matching the documented the RTX 5090 host's Linux distro alias; host key re-verified out of band and re-pinned on the workstation

per-host ed25519 replica keys on all three Windows hosts and inside the WSL distro, cross-authorized with no-pty/no-forwarding restrictions and host keys pinned, so any fleet host can address any other over the tailnet
